headline: High-risk shared-file and tool-use overlap: open-webui can ingest Khoj outputs and both can expose sensitive notes, documents, and API keys.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and open-webui can use MCP, OpenAPI tools, plugins, and function calling. If Khoj content is surfaced into open-webui, prompt-like text in notes or retrieved documents can steer tool use. The pair lacks a documented isolation/provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF Khoj outputs are copied or retrieved into open-webui prompts without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF open-webui tool calls are enabled against content sourced from Khoj, attacker-controlled note text can influence actions.
mitigations: Disable tool use for untrusted retrieved text.
Add a provenance tag to Khoj-derived snippets before passing them onward.
Require human review before any tool call triggered by retrieved content.
Restrict open-webui to read-only workflows for Khoj-fed sessions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while open-webui touches files, notes, documents, persistent memory, and API keys. Both have broad network egress and file access surfaces, so a shared workspace or copied context can leak sensitive data into open-webui outputs or upstream APIs. The pairwise path is credible without extra safeguards.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same notes/files directory, leakage risk is present.
IF open-webui sends retrieved Khoj content to a third-party model API, sensitive notes can leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate the two agents onto different workspaces.
Remove API keys from open-webui sessions that process Khoj data.
Turn on offline/local-only mode for open-webui when handling sensitive notes.
Limit Khoj indexing to non-sensitive folders.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read filesystem content and open-webui can read local files and mounted volumes, while open-webui also supports persistent shared sessions. If both are aimed at the same mutable directory or shared data volume, they can race on the same artifacts even though Khoj does not write files. Uncertainty about orchestration means the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF both agents are configured against the same mounted volume, concurrent reads can conflict with user edits or cleanup workflows.
IF open-webui writes artifacts into a directory Khoj indexes, stale or inconsistent state can arise.
mitigations: Point each agent at separate directories.
Make the shared directory read-only for one agent.
Schedule non-overlapping access windows.
Use a staging folder for open-webui artifacts before Khoj indexing.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent over personal notes and documents, and open-webui can act on tool outputs via plugins, MCP, and function calling. If open-webui treats Khoj-derived answers as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or generated content. The interaction is plausible by default and can affect multiple work products.
conditions: IF open-webui uses Khoj answers as direct inputs to tools or generated artifacts without verification, cascading errors can propagate.
IF Khoj retrieval returns stale or incomplete notes, open-webui may operationalize them.
mitigations: Require citation checks before open-webui acts on Khoj output.
Insert a verification step that compares retrieved facts to source documents.
Disable autonomous tool execution for Khoj-sourced answers.
Log and review any downstream action based on retrieved content.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while open-webui touches persistent memory, usage analytics, model evaluation data, files, and API keys. Their documented data classes and retention-like surfaces differ, so combining them can create compliance mismatches even without a named residency violation. The other agent is cited because the mismatch is pairwise, not single-agent.
conditions: IF the same personal notes are processed by both agents, retention and logging policies must align.
IF open-webui analytics or memory retain Khoj-derived content longer than Khoj's storage policy, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Document a shared retention policy.
Disable analytics for sensitive sessions.
Purge open-webui memory after each Khoj-assisted task.
Restrict API-key-bearing sessions from processing personal notes.
